newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria plans gendarmerie force to fight crime.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria plans gendarmerie force to fight crime.

text.p: Bulgaria plans to establish a national gendarmerie to guard strategic sites and help fight crime, an interior ministry official said on Tuesday.

Ministry secretary Lyutskan Lyutskanov said interior ministry troops currently used to guard embassies and consulates would be transformed into a paramilitary police force modelled on the French gendarmerie as part of the ministry's restructuring.

"The functions of the gendarmerie are included in a draft law for security and social order in Bulgaria, which will be presented to the Council of Ministers next week," Lyutskanov told a news conference.
The new law also needs the approval of parliament.
Lyutskanov said some interior ministry units deployed since the communist era in areas populated by ethnic Turks were idle.
He said that by September or October gendarmerie units would start guarding industrial sites and oil pipelines.
Among the sites will be the Kozloduy nuclear power plant, the Maritsa East coal mining and thermal power complex, military plants in the towns of Kazanlak and Sopot and the Neftochim oil refinery.
Gendarmerie units will be also located in the country's biggest towns and will help other services in maintaining order and fighting crime.
